questions.prompt: Prices A and B both give large ADF p-values on their own. The spread A - 1.5 × B gives a coint p-value of 0.0026. What do you conclude?
options: The pair is not cointegrated, because each price wanders
The pair looks cointegrated: each price wanders, but the spread is stationary
Price A causes price B to move
questions.explanation: Cointegration means exactly this: each price wanders on its own, but a combination of them returns to its mean. A coint p-value below 0.05 is evidence for that.

questions.prompt: Why does coint report a larger p-value (0.0026) than a plain adfuller on the same fitted spread (0.0005)?
options: coint uses fewer days of data
The hedge ratio was chosen to make the spread look calm, so coint uses stricter thresholds to make up for it
questions.explanation: Fitting the hedge ratio on the same data makes the spread look as stable as possible. The Engle-Granger test allows for that choice, so its p-value is the honest one.

questions.prompt: The hedge ratio of a pair is 1.5. What does that mean?
options: You pair 1.5 shares of B with each share of A to form the spread
Price A is always 1.5 dollars above price B
The spread closes 1.5 times per month
questions.explanation: The hedge ratio h is the slope of the best straight line through the prices. The spread is A - h × B, so h is the number of B shares paired with one share of A.
